To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) NBTI from ISSG is better than that of the furnace process; (b) PDA can significantly reduce NBTI; (c) DPN improves NBTI; and (d) nitrogen concentration can be used as an additional parameter in the NBTI model to better understand the DPN process.
the NBTIs of the devices from ISSG process is better than those from the Gox1 process, PDA can significantly reduce the NBTI and DPN can significantly improve NBITI.

the NBTIs (negative bias temperature instabilities) from ISSG and DPN processes are much better than those from furnace Gox1 processes and that the NBTi performance is significantly improved with a higher PDA temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the NBTI degradation in the 28 nm HKMG p-MOSET process, including the I/O oxide process, PDA, and DPN.
the influence of the I/O oxide process, and the results provide useful guidance for process optimization.
the influence of the I/O oxide processes on the NBTIs performance and provides a better understanding of the NBTI mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NBTIs from the devices with DPN process are much better than those from the devices with non-DPN processes.
the DPN process can improve the NBTI reliability of I/O devices.
the NBTi performance is strongly related to the I/O oxide process and the DPN is the key process in the I/O oxide stack.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NBT1 performance of the I/O thick oxide HKMG p-MOSTs can be improved through ISSG, PDA, and DPN processes.

the NBTIs from different I/O processes are quite different and the NBTI can be significantly improved by PDA and DPN processes, which is important for the design and process development for the I/O p-MOSFETS.
the NBTIs from the I/O thick oxide process with the DPN process and the PDA process are the best among all the processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the I/O oxide process has a strong impact on the NBTIDP (nitrogen induced degradation of positive bias temperature instability) of 28  nm HfO _{2} -based HKMG I/O thick oxide devices.
the NBTIs of I/O devices can be improved by using ISSG, furnace Gox1, and DPN process.
the NBTIDPN model provides a much clearer direction on how to optimize the DPN process to achieve the best reliability performance.
